hero.title: Human Reproduction — The Complete Journey
hero.hook: Every human alive is the result of one sperm out of hundreds of millions reaching one egg, fertilising it, and that single cell dividing billions of times to become a person. Human reproduction is one of the most detailed, precisely orchestrated biological processes — and one of the most consistently tested topics in Class 12 Biology.

hook_section.scenario: The human reproductive process is surprisingly complex: male produces millions of sperm daily via spermatogenesis; female produces one egg per month via oogenesis; the egg is released at ovulation and must be fertilised within 12–24 hours; the sperm must travel from vagina through uterus to fallopian tube within 72 hours; fertilisation occurs in the fallopian tube; implantation takes 6–10 days. Miss any step, and reproduction fails.
hook_section.bridge: Chapter 3 covers the male and female reproductive systems, gametogenesis (spermatogenesis + oogenesis), fertilisation, implantation, placenta, embryonic development, and parturition. Many students confuse spermatogenesis with oogenesis — this week's focus makes it clear.
hook_section.punchline: Spermatogenesis (continuous in males, from puberty). Oogenesis (starts before birth, resumes at puberty, completes only if fertilised). These parallel processes are the most exam-intensive part.

concept_section.analogy: Think of spermatogenesis like a factory running 24/7 — continuously producing millions of units (sperm) per day. Oogenesis is like a unique artisan workshop — it starts making a product before the workshop even opens (before birth), pauses production for years, resumes slowly releasing one item per month (ovulation), and only finishes the product if a buyer shows up (fertilisation). Different timelines, different outputs, same purpose.
concept_section.principle: Spermatogenesis: spermatogonia (2n) → primary spermatocyte (2n) → [meiosis I] secondary spermatocytes (n) → [meiosis II] spermatids (n) → spermatozoa. Oogenesis: oogonia (2n) → primary oocyte (2n, arrested in prophase I from foetal life) → [at puberty, meiosis I completes] secondary oocyte (n) + first polar body → [after fertilisation, meiosis II completes] ovum (n) + second polar body.
concept_section.reveal_prompt: Tap each section to explore reproductive biology 👇

reveals.question: ♂️ Male reproductive system?
reveals.answer: Testes (in scrotal sac, 2–2.5°C below body temperature for spermatogenesis) → seminiferous tubules (sperm production) → epididymis (maturation and storage) → vas deferens → seminal vesicle + prostate + bulbourethral gland (accessory glands) → urethra. Testosterone produced by Leydig cells.

reveals.question: ♀️ Female reproductive system?
reveals.answer: Ovaries (ovum production + oestrogen/progesterone) → fallopian tubes (site of fertilisation) → uterus (implantation, foetal development) → cervix → vagina. Graafian follicle in ovary contains the secondary oocyte. Ovulation = Graafian follicle ruptures, releasing secondary oocyte.

reveals.question: 🌱 Fertilisation to implantation?
reveals.answer: Fertilisation: sperm meets secondary oocyte in fallopian tube → triggers meiosis II completion → ovum forms → sperm nucleus + ovum nucleus fuse → zygote (2n). Cleavage: zygote divides → 2 cells → 4 → 8 → morula (16-cell solid ball) → blastocyst (hollow). Implantation: blastocyst embeds in uterine wall (endometrium) 6–10 days after fertilisation.

reveals.question: 🤱 Placenta and parturition?
reveals.answer: Placenta: exchange of nutrients, O₂, CO₂ between mother and foetus; produces hCG (detected in pregnancy tests), oestrogen, progesterone. Parturition (childbirth): triggered by oxytocin from posterior pituitary; stimulates uterine contractions; positive feedback loop. Normal gestation period = 9 months (38 weeks).

points: Spermatogenesis: continuous in males; spermatogonia → (meiosis) → 4 spermatids → 4 spermatozoa
Oogenesis: 1 oocyte → 1 ovum + 3 polar bodies; primary oocyte arrested in prophase I from foetal life
Fertilisation: occurs in fallopian tube; secondary oocyte completes meiosis II only after sperm entry
Implantation: blastocyst embeds in endometrium; triggers placenta formation
Placenta: secretes hCG, maintains pregnancy; exchange organ between mother and foetus

quiz.q: Fertilisation in humans occurs in the:
quiz.exp: Fertilisation takes place in the fallopian tube (oviduct), specifically in the ampullary-isthmic junction. The fertilised egg (zygote) then travels to the uterus for implantation.

quiz.q: How many spermatozoa are produced from one primary spermatocyte?
quiz.exp: One primary spermatocyte (2n) → meiosis I → 2 secondary spermatocytes (n) → meiosis II → 4 spermatids → 4 spermatozoa. All 4 are functional.

quiz.q: The site of testosterone production in the testis is:
quiz.exp: Testosterone is produced by interstitial cells of Leydig (Leydig cells) located between the seminiferous tubules. Sertoli cells provide nourishment to developing sperms.

quiz.q: Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG) is secreted by:
quiz.exp: hCG is secreted by the placenta (trophoblast cells). It maintains the corpus luteum during early pregnancy to keep producing progesterone. hCG in urine is detected by pregnancy tests.

flipcards.back: Fallopian tube (oviduct) — specifically the ampullary region

flipcards.front: What is the ploidy of a secondary oocyte?
flipcards.back: Haploid (n) — it has completed meiosis I but meiosis II completes only after fertilisation

flipcards.front: What hormone does the placenta produce?
flipcards.back: hCG (human Chorionic Gonadotropin), oestrogen, progesterone, human Placental Lactogen (hPL)
About 9 months (38 weeks / 266 days from fertilisation; 280 days from last menstrual period)
First milk secreted by mammary glands after childbirth — rich in antibodies (IgA), proteins and nutrients. Essential for newborn immunity.
Oxytocin from posterior pituitary — stimulates uterine contractions. Positive feedback: more contractions → more oxytocin.
